concerns.text: FR-009 currently reads “System MUST compute the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) … (See SC‑009)”. It does not reference any User Story, so the functional requirement is orphaned. It should be anchored to the comparative‑evaluation story (US‑03), e.g., “(See US‑03)”.

SC-007 states “Richness assessment: FID … (See SC‑009)”. This success criterion is not tied to any User Story, making it an orphan. It should reference US‑03 (or the appropriate story) instead of another SC, e.g., “(See US‑03)”.

FR-009 cross‑references SC‑009 (a Success Criterion) instead of a User Story or appropriate source; functional requirements should reference the source of the requirement (e.g., a user story or design spec), not a success‑criteria metric definition.

Inconsistent terminology for the physics teacher signal: both “physics‑teacher” (with hyphen) and “physics teacher” (without hyphen) are used interchangeably, which may cause ambiguity in traceability and downstream tooling.

FR-007 requires training the neural‑teacher baseline on the *original Causal Forcing++ dataset*, but the specification provides no source, access method, or size for that dataset. Without a reachable, verifiable dataset the requirement cannot be exercised, making the functional requirement untestable.

FR-007 requires the neural‑teacher baseline to be trained on the *original Causal Forcing++ dataset*, yet the plan substitutes the same synthetic physics dataset because the original dataset is unavailable. This creates a mismatch: the physics‑teacher model and the neural‑teacher baseline are trained on different data distributions, but US‑03 and SC‑004 assume a paired t‑test on *the same test sequences*. Comparing models trained on non‑identical training data violates the independence of the validation target from the predictor and renders the statistical significance claim invalid.

Inconsistent terminology for the physics teacher signal: both “physics‑teacher” (with hyphen) and “physics teacher” (without hyphen) are used interchangeably, which may cause ambiguity in traceability and downstream tooling.
